entry_text: Can't focus on the Statistics module again. I keep hearing my old position coach in my head telling me I was never a numbers guy, I was a hit-first guy. Retaking Stats through UNF's online program for the third time. The football camp is this weekend so I'll miss both live tutoring sessions. I told my advisor the degree would take care of itself and it is not taking care of itself.
Live tutoring session missed (no-show).
Assignment 3 (Statistics) submitted 4 days late.

Read the academic warning letter out loud to my wife. It says term GPA 2.1 and one more failing grade puts me on probation. I played three seasons at linebacker and never got benched and now a Stats class is benching me. The daughter's daycare pickup is on me Thursdays so that tutoring slot is gone too.

The professor wrote on my last quiz: 'You are guessing, not reasoning. Come to office hours or this will not improve.' I have not gone to office hours. I do appearances on weekends and run the youth camp and I am tired in a way office hours will not fix.

Three sessions missed this week. I feel like I already failed and I'm just watching it happen. Wrote eleven bullet points for a camp speech instead of doing the problem set. Priorities are backwards, I know.
Quiz score 52% (Statistics, Module 4).

Cancelled the subscription back on April 4 and the access runs out at the end of the billing period. If I'm going to fail Stats I don't need to pay $39 a month to watch myself fail it. Advisor said it would look good. It does not look like anything.
Paid access ended at billing-period close (subscription cancelled Apr 04; churned).

The N2 cohort is hard after teaching all day. I'm the only American in the Tuesday-night group and the tutor uses my first name on the recording. I stared at one grammar point for two hours tonight and it would not resolve. Passed N3 in December so I know I can do this, but N2 is a different animal.
Studied the kanji deck until 1 AM. Setagaya is quiet at night which helps. The July exam is the whole reason I subscribed. I keep the streak going even when the eikaiwa shift wrecks me.
Study session logged (48 min, JLPT N2 track).
Assignment 2 submitted on time.

Moved to Tokyo from Portland two years ago on the teaching visa and this exam is the thing I'm doing for me. The tutor said my listening jumped a level. I opened the practice-quiz feature four times this week. It's becoming the good part of the day.
Quiz 78% on the N2 grammar set. Best yet. Renewed for another quarter without thinking about it.
Practice-quiz feature opened 4 times this week.
Two sessions attended this week, both on time. The routine is working. I want to sit N2 in July and not flinch.
Study session logged (41 min, quantitative-methods add-on).

Up early before the Senate office opens. Cleared the quant-methods problem set for the MPA before the kids are awake. Ohio University second year, GPA 3.7, and the only thing standing between me and a 4.0 is regression analysis, which is why I bought the tutoring add-on.
Long day scheduling for the Senator. Still made the 7pm live tutoring session. Partner is on nights this week so I had both kids at the table doing homework while I did mine.
Assignment 4 submitted on time.

The quant add-on is worth it. The tutor walked me through the standard-error thing I kept missing. I logged in from the office after everyone left. This subscription pays for itself if it gets me the 4.0.
Quiz score 91% (quant methods).
Attended the live session again. Four in a row now. Renewed the annual plan — cheaper than monthly and I'm not going anywhere until this MPA is done.
Live tutoring session attended (on time).
Practice-problem feature opened 6 times this week.
Assignment 5 submitted on time.
Study session logged (39 min).

Atmospheric Dynamics I broke me last term. I failed it, term GPA 1.8, and the probation letter came in January. I'm the weekend morning meteorologist at the station and management said I need the FSU degree for the chief-meteorologist opening, so the stakes are not abstract. I missed both tutoring sessions this week because of the 4 AM on-air call time.

Read the academic probation letter again. It says one more term below 2.0 and I'm dismissed from the distance program. I have a son, twelve, shared custody, and the weeks he's with me the late-night study sessions just do not happen.
Live tutoring session missed (no-show).
Assignment 3 submitted 3 days late.

The professor's comment on my dynamics problem set: 'This is memorized, not understood — you will not pass the final this way.' She's right and it stings because I explain weather to a whole city every Saturday morning. I closed the app for four days after reading it.

The station has an extended-time accommodation letter on file with the university for my documented ADHD, but it doesn't help when I physically cannot be awake at midnight after a 4 AM call time. I logged into the practice feature zero times this week.
Subscription downgraded to free tier (churned from paid).

Downgraded to the free tier on the 25th. If I'm going to lose the tutoring anyway I'd rather stop paying $39 a month while I'm on probation. I want the chief job. I am not sure I want it enough to survive Dynamics II.

Coding bootcamp track, week six, and I actually finished the JavaScript project tonight. Baby was up till 11 so my partner took the first shift and I coded 11 to 1. The toddler is up at 6:20 like clockwork. Submitted on time somehow.

The bootcamp mentor said my last project was 'the strongest in the cohort this week,' which I did not expect as a 34-year-old career-changer with two kids. I opened the practice-problem feature five times this week between feedings. It's the one hour that's mine.
Assignment 5 submitted on time.
Study session logged (44 min).
Quiz 88% on the async-JavaScript module. Renewed the subscription for another quarter. This is the thing that gets me out of the job I'm leaving, so the $39 is not up for debate.
I keep the streak going even on two hours of sleep. The mentor feedback is what does it — someone telling me the code is good. I attended both live sessions this week.
Live tutoring session attended (on time).
Practice-problem feature opened 5 times this week.

GED math track. The suspension from my old high school in 2015 is why I'm doing this at 23 through the community program instead of a diploma. I lay on the floor with the lights off tonight because the fractions module came back marked 'incomplete' again and I do not know how to make it complete.

Couldn't sleep, couldn't study. My head gets loud when I haven't talked to anyone for two days and I haven't talked to anyone for two days. The GED is the thing that's supposed to fix the suspension, undo it, and some nights it just feels like proof of the suspension.
Live tutoring session missed (no-show).

Slept till 1pm, missed the morning session. The GED math deadline through the program is overdue. Messaged the tutor to move Wednesday to Thursday. She always says yes. I don't know what I'd do without that flexibility.

The counselor at the GED program says the thing where I imagine just not showing up to any of it — not the tutoring, not the test, not any of it — is not the same as actually meaning to quit. The thought just visits. I told her about it last month. I think about that a lot.
Assignment 2 submitted 5 days late.
Practice-problem feature opened 0 times this week.
Study session logged (52 min, MCAT organic-chemistry track).

Erg practice at 5:45 with the rowing team, then straight to the o-chem module. Retaking organic chemistry for the MCAT and the tutoring add-on is the only reason the reaction mechanisms are sticking. Coach knows the MCAT comes first this term but the scholarship depends on me staying on the boat.

Named-university scholarship rower, which sounds glamorous until you're doing o-chem flashcards on the bus back from a regatta. Attended the live tutoring session between practice and lab. Four in a row now.

The worry is always the scholarship. If the o-chem grade drops, the GPA drops, and if the GPA drops the athletic scholarship is in question, and without it I can't afford to be here at all. So I open the practice feature every day and I do not miss sessions. The subscription is the cheapest insurance I have.
Quiz score 84% (organic chemistry).
Renewed the annual plan. Between rowing and the MCAT I'm not shopping for tutors mid-season. Attended the session again.
Live tutoring session attended (on time).
Practice-problem feature opened 6 times this week.

Just got home from the overnight warehouse shift. Both kids asleep on the couch. Degree-completion track and I have not opened the module in a week. Alarm at 6:20 for school drop. This is the Tuesday-Wednesday rotation and it means the two live tutoring sessions are always at hours I'm either working or driving.
Live tutoring session missed (no-show).
Assignment 4 not submitted (past due).

Cancelled the subscription back on March 29 but the account still works on some free trial. I don't know for how long. I will not pay $39 a month to be told my coursework is behind. I know it's behind.

The 9-year-old asked if I was sad. I said just tired. Between the warehouse and the school runs there is no hour left for the degree, and the eviction notice at the last apartment did not help. We're moving into my sister's place end of the month. Fourth address this year.
Practice-problem feature opened 0 times this week.

Missed the third session in a row. Sometimes between warehouse shifts I think about just letting the whole degree go, not withdrawing formally, just never logging in again. I won't. The kids are watching. But I think about it.

Closed the bar at 2, walked home. Degree-completion track, 41 years old, and the shift work means every live session is scheduled for a time I'm behind a bar. Missed both this week. The one thing keeping me enrolled is stubbornness.
Live tutoring session missed (no-show).
Assignment 3 submitted 6 days late.

Same story. Closed late, slept late, missed the morning module. A regular tipped me a hundred on a forty-dollar tab and asked if I'd thought about going back to school full-time. I said I'm trying to finish this one class part-time and even that is losing to the bar schedule.

Quiz came back 49%. It crosses my mind walking home that if I just stopped logging in, none of the Tuesday deadline stuff would have to happen. I don't want to quit. I want to want it again. There's a difference.
Subscription cancelled (churned).
Cancelled on the 24th after the 49% quiz. My sister said I should call the academic advisor before I fully quit. I said I would. I probably won't.
Studying in the cab tonight at the truck stop in Lordsburg NM. 11 hours of driving today, another 11 tomorrow. Degree-completion track. Logged a short study session on the phone before lights out.
Study session logged (22 min, mobile).

Long empty stretch of I-10 east of El Paso, nothing to do but think. Went back to school at 52 after the divorce because the only thing I built in all those years was a house someone else lives in now. The tutoring sessions are all scheduled for daytime hours I'm driving, so I do the async modules at truck stops instead.
Assignment 2 submitted 1 day late.

Missed the live session again — can't attend a 2pm anything from the cab. But I opened the practice-problem feature twice this week at the Flying J. The mobile stuff is the only reason I'm still enrolled at all.

Downgraded to the free tier on April 14 because I can't use the live tutoring the plan is built around. I keep the account because the async quizzes tell me I'm still moving, even 22 minutes at a time. That's sometimes the difference between staying enrolled and not.
Study session logged (37 min, data-analytics track).

Run, 5K, 24:50. Then opened the data-analytics module at 6:40. Career-changer after the October layoff, using the bootcamp track to pivot into analytics. Two live sessions this week, both attended. The structure is the only thing holding my days together right now.

Six months since the layoff and the bootcamp is the thing I point to when people at church ask what I'm doing. The mentor said my SQL project was 'interview-ready.' I opened the practice feature five times this week. Job screens are finally coming.
Assignment 4 submitted on time.
Quiz 82% on the data-cleaning module. Renewed the subscription. The old me applied to 67 jobs with a finance résumé; the new me is going to apply with a portfolio, and this track is the portfolio.
Live tutoring session attended (on time).
Practice-problem feature opened 5 times this week.

A recruiter sent a screener link for Tuesday. Ran 8K to celebrate, then logged the assignment. Attended both sessions this week. 67 applications, 4 screens — the analytics track is what finally changed the math.

Capstone due in 19 days for the online master's. Wrote committee responses till 1. Stopped because my hands were shaking again, the way they shake when I skip a meal, which I did today. Submitted the draft section on time though.

Panic about the capstone hit around 11:30. Lasted twenty minutes. The breathing thing the university counseling center taught me actually worked tonight. Not always. Tonight. I still made the deadline.
Assignment 6 submitted on time.
Study session logged (48 min, capstone track).

University counseling 4pm, weekly. Talked about pacing the capstone. She asked if the late-night study schedule is making the anxiety worse. I said yes. I will not change the schedule before the capstone is done. We both know that.

The triple-decker is loud after midnight when both roommates are home, so I work at the kitchen table with that white noise. Attended the live tutoring session this week and opened the practice feature four times. The routine holds even when the anxiety doesn't.
Downgraded to the tutoring-only tier on the 18th — can't afford the full subscription on the grad stipend. The tier I kept still gives me the capstone tutoring, which is the part I actually need.
My advisor sent capstone edits at 11pm. Of course he did. I will read them at 8 AM with coffee, not at 11 PM half-panicked. That's a rule I'm trying to keep. Session attended, assignment in.
